where: Harness sidebar selectors and Command-O input/scroll surfaces
what: Andrew requested model/effort selection directly on each sidebar row, a local-machine icon beside the hostname, and a real caret plus scrolling in search. The earlier search field was only drawn text and the results swapped a fixed eight-row slice.
cost: The installed UI lacked ordinary editing and mouse/trackpad behavior despite displaying a search field.
cause: A manually maintained query string and sliced result rows stood in for the existing editor and scroll primitives. Model identity and model selection lived in different sidebar locations.
whys: The field displayed Text without owning a text editor or selection.
Typing only appended and erasing only popped the query.
Only a bounded visible slice existed, so there was no scrollable result content.
The recognition label and its selector were implemented separately.
The view used text-shaped placeholders for interactive primitives rather than sharing the editor, scroll surface and selector state.
class: An interactive-looking control is rendered as static text or a manual slice, without the primitive that owns its interaction.
prevention: Palette query is now the shared Draft editor with TextEdit, IME, pointer and clipboard routing. Full bounded results and the preview each use the existing scroll surface/physics, with modal input ownership and selected-row reveal. Sidebar identity and selection share the same row targets and picker state.
fix: Model and effort are separate inline hit targets; the bottom model control is removed. The local device header has a computer icon and an explicit connection tooltip. Native scene tests and offscreen clicks, selection, I-beam hover and independent wheel gestures verify the interaction.
